facts.statement: Thecodontosaurus was a small bipedal animal approximately 2 meters long.
facts.quote: Thecodontosaurus was a small bipedal animal, about 2 m long.

facts.statement: The name Thecodontosaurus means "socket-tooth" because its teeth were positioned in separate sockets rather than being fused to the jaw bone.
facts.quote: The name is derived from Greek θήκή, , "socket", and οδους, , "tooth", a reference to the fact that the roots of the teeth were not fused with the jaw bone, as in present lizards, but positioned in separate tooth sockets.

facts.statement: The genus Thecodontosaurus was named in 1836 by Henry Riley and Samuel Stutchbury.
facts.quote: In 1836, naming a new genus: Thecodontosaurus.

facts.statement: John Morris provided the complete species name Thecodontosaurus antiquus in 1843.
facts.quote: In 1843, in his catalogue of British fossils, John Morris provided a complete species name: Thecodontosaurus antiquus.

facts.statement: Peter Galton designated a right dentary as the neotype for Thecodontosaurus in 1985.
facts.quote: In 1985, Peter Galton designated another lower jaw, a right dentary, as the neotype, BCM 2.

facts.statement: Remains of Thecodontosaurus are primarily found in Triassic fissure fillings in southern England.
facts.quote: Its remains are known mostly from Triassic "fissure fillings" in southern England.

facts.statement: Thecodontosaurus lived between 206 and 201 million years ago during the Rhaetian age in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Triásico, entre 206 a 201 durante el Rhaetiense, en lo que hoy es Europa.

facts.statement: Thecodontosaurus possessed many small to medium-sized, serrated, leaf-shaped teeth in its jaws.
facts.quote: Its jaws contained many small- to medium-sized, serrated, leaf-shaped teeth.

facts.statement: Thecodontosaurus had five digits on its hands and feet, with long, narrow hands featuring an extended claw on each.
facts.quote: This dinosaur's hands and feet each had five digits, and the hands were long and rather narrow, with an extended claw on each.

facts.statement: On average, Thecodontosaurus was 1.2 meters long, 30 centimeters tall, and weighed 11 kilograms.
facts.quote: On average, it was 1.2 m long, 30 cm or 1 ft. tall, and weighed 11 kg.

facts.statement: The largest known individuals of Thecodontosaurus reached an estimated length of 2.5 meters.
facts.quote: The largest individuals had an estimated length of 2.5 m.

facts.statement: Muscle attachment studies suggest Thecodontosaurus was an extremely fast bipedal runner that used its weaker front limbs to grasp and process vegetation.
facts.quote: Studies of the muscle attachments in its fore and hindlimbs suggest that it was an extremely fast bipedal runner that relied on its weaker front limbs for grasping vegetation, cutting it up and feeding it into its mouth.

facts.statement: Researchers explain the small size of Thecodontosaurus as an instance of insular dwarfism.
facts.quote: The small size has been explained as an instance of insular dwarfism.

facts.statement: In 2000, Michael Benton suggested that a robust morph found in the population might represent either a second species or sexual dimorphism.
facts.quote: In 2000, Michael Benton noted the existence of a robust morph in the population, seen by him as a possible second species or, more likely, an instance of sexual dimorphism.

facts.statement: Thomas Huxley was the first to recognize Thecodontosaurus as a dinosaur in 1870, though he incorrectly placed it in the Scelidosauridae.
facts.quote: It was not until 1870 that Thomas Huxley became the first person to understand that it was a dinosaur, though referring it incorrectly to the Scelidosauridae.

facts.statement: Modern cladistic analyses have not been conclusive, but Thecodontosaurus is often placed in a basal position among sauropodomorph dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Modern exact cladistic analyses have not been conclusive. Although not actually the earliest member of the group, Thecodontosaurus is sometimes placed in a very basal position among the sauropodomorph dinosaurs.

facts.statement: The hypothesis that carnivorous prosauropods with the body of Thecodontosaurus and slicing teeth existed has been totally discredited.
facts.quote: the hypothesis that such creatures existed has now been totally discredited.

facts.statement: Harry Govier Seeley named Agrosaurus macgillivrayi in 1891, mistakenly believing the remains were collected in Australia.
facts.quote: In 1891, Harry Govier Seeley named Agrosaurus macgillivrayi, assuming the remains had been collected in 1844 by the crew of HMS Fly on the northeast coast of Australia.

facts.statement: In 2020, Ballell, Rayfield, and Benton suggested that Pantydraco caducus might be a taxon of uncertain validity or a juvenile of Thecodontosaurus antiquus.
facts.quote: However, Ballell, Rayfield & Benton (2020) considered Pantydraco caducus to be a taxon of uncertain validity, and considered it possible that it might represent a juvenile of Thecodontosaurus antiquus.

facts.statement: The largest individuals of Thecodontosaurus reached an estimated length of 2.5 meters.
facts.quote: Los individuos más grandes tenían una longitud estimada de 2,5 metros (8,2 pies).

facts.statement: Thecodontosaurus possessed a narrow skull equipped with curved teeth.
facts.quote: Poseía un cráneo estrecho dotado de dientes curvos.

facts.statement: Its jaws contained many small to medium-sized, leaf-shaped, serrated teeth.
facts.quote: Sus mandíbulas contenían muchos dientes en forma de hoja, aserrados y de tamaño pequeño a mediano.

facts.statement: The dinosaur had five-fingered hands and feet, with long, narrow hands featuring an extended claw on each.
facts.quote: Las manos y los pies de este dinosaurio tenían cinco dedos cada uno, y las manos eran largas y bastante estrechas, con una garra extendida en cada una.

facts.statement: Its front limbs were much shorter than its legs, and its tail was longer than the combined length of its head, neck, and body.
facts.quote: Las extremidades delanteras de este dinosaurio eran mucho más cortas que las piernas, y su cola era mucho más larga que la cabeza, el cuello y el cuerpo juntos.

facts.statement: Examination revealed that Thecodontosaurus was exclusively bipedal.
facts.quote: El examen de Thecodontosaurus reveló que era exclusivamente bípedo.

facts.statement: Muscle insertion studies suggest it was an extremely fast bipedal runner that used its weaker front limbs to grasp, cut, and carry vegetation to its mouth.
facts.quote: Los estudios de las inserciones musculares en sus extremidades delanteras y traseras sugieren que era un corredor bípedo extremadamente rápido que dependía de sus extremidades delanteras más débiles para agarrar la vegetación, cortarla y llevársela a la boca.

facts.statement: In autumn 1834, surgeon Henry Riley and Bristol Institution curator Samuel Stutchbury began excavating "sauroid remains" at the Durdham Down quarry in Clifton, now part of Bristol.
facts.quote: En el otoño de 1834, el cirujano Henry Riley y el curador de la Institución de Bristol, Samuel Stutchbury, comenzaron a excavar "restos de saurio" en la cantera de Durdham Down, en Clifton , actualmente parte de Bristol, que forma parte del Conglomerado de Magnesia.

facts.statement: They provided an initial description in 1836, naming a new genus without a species, Thecodontosaurus.
facts.quote: En 1836, nombrando un nuevo género, sin especie, Thecodontosaurus .

facts.statement: The name derives from Greek words meaning "socket" and "tooth," referencing that tooth roots were not fused to the jawbone but placed in separate dental cavities.
facts.quote: El nombre se deriva del griego θήκή, thēkē, "enchufe", y οδους, odorus, "diente", una referencia al hecho de que las raíces de los dientes no estaban fusionadas con el hueso de la mandíbula, como en los lagartos actuales, sino colocadas en cavidades dentales separadas.

facts.statement: In 1843, John Morris provided the full species name Thecodontosaurus antiquus in his catalog of British fossils.
facts.quote: En 1843, en su catálogo de fósiles británicos, John Morris proporcionó un nombre de especie completo, Thecodontosaurus antiquus.

facts.statement: The first specimen was described and named based on a jaw fragment discovered in Bristol, southwest England.
facts.quote: El primer espécimen fue descrito y nombrado a partir de un fragmento de mandíbula descubierto al suroeste de Inglaterra, en la localidad de Bristol.

facts.statement: Fossil remains of Thecodontosaurus and related material were destroyed in 1940 during World War II bombing raids.
facts.quote: Los restos fósiles de Thecodontosaurus, y otro material relacionado, fueron destruidos en 1940, en los bombardeos de la Segunda Guerra Mundial.

facts.statement: Today, 184 fossil bones are part of the collection at the Bristol City Museum and Art Gallery.
facts.quote: Hoy en día, 184 huesos fósiles forman parte de la colección del Museo y Galería de Arte de la Ciudad de Bristol.

facts.statement: In 1985, Peter Galton designated another lower jaw, a right dentary, as the neotype, BCM 2.
facts.quote: En 1985, Peter Galton designó otro maxilar inferior, un dentario derecho, como el neotipo, BCM 2.

facts.statement: While once thought to date to the late Carnian, recent studies indicate these deposits date to the Rhaetian.
facts.quote: La edad de estos depósitos se estimó alguna vez como a fines del Carniense , pero estudios recientes indican que datan del Rético.

facts.statement: It appears some of these small dinosaurs fell into rock crevices while passing over the Upper Triassic limestone surface.
facts.quote: Al parecer algunos de estos pequeños dinosaurios cayeron en grietas rocosas al pasar por la superficie caliza del Triásico Superior.

facts.statement: Its small size has been explained as a case of insular dwarfism.
facts.quote: El pequeño tamaño se ha explicado como un caso de enanismo insular.

facts.statement: In 2000, Michael Benton noted a robust morph in the population, viewing it as either a possible second species or more likely a case of sexual dimorphism.
facts.quote: En 2000, Michael Benton notó la existencia de un morfo robusto en la población, visto por él como una posible segunda especie o, más probablemente, un caso de dimorfismo sexual.

facts.statement: Currently, the only valid species is T. antiquus.
facts.quote: Actualmente, la única especie válida es T. antiquus.

facts.statement: Although defended by Michael Cooper in 1981, the hypothesis that such creatures existed has now been totally discredited.
facts.quote: Aunque aún defendida por Michael Cooper en 1981, la hipótesis de que tales criaturas existieron ahora ha sido totalmente desacreditada.

facts.statement: In 1999 it was discovered that the bones likely belonged to a batch sent by Riley and Stutchbury to the British Museum of Natural History and then mislabeled.
facts.quote: En 1999 se descubrió que los huesos probablemente pertenecían a un lote enviado por Riley y Stutchbury al Museo Británico de Historia Natural y luego mal etiquetado.

facts.statement: In 2007 it became the separate genus Pantydraco caducus.
facts.quote: En 2007 se convirtió en el género separado Pantydraco caducus.

facts.statement: However, in 2020 Ballell, Rayfield, and Benton considered P. caducus a taxon of uncertain validity and suggested it might represent a juvenile of Thecodontosaurus antiquus.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, Ballell, Rayfield & Benton en 2020 consideraron a P. caducus como un taxón de validez incierta, y consideraron posible que pudiera representar un juvenil de Thecodontosaurus antiquus.

facts.statement: Thecodontosaurus was originally classified by Riley and Stutchbury as a member of Squamata, the group containing lizards and snakes.
facts.quote: Riley y Stutchbury originalmente vieron a Thecodontosaurus como miembro de Squamata, el grupo que contiene lagartos y serpientes.

facts.statement: When Richard Owen coined the term Dinosauria in 1842, he did not recognize Thecodontosaurus as a dinosaur.
facts.quote: Richard Owen acuñó el término Dinosauria en 1842, porque Owen no reconoció a Thecodontosaurus como un dinosaurio.

facts.statement: In 1865, the animal was assigned to the group Thecodontia.
facts.quote: En 1865, lo asignó a Thecodontia.

facts.statement: Thomas Huxley was the first person to understand that Thecodontosaurus was a dinosaur in 1870.
facts.quote: No fue hasta 1870 que Thomas Huxley se convirtió en la primera persona en comprender que se trataba de un dinosaurio

facts.statement: Later, the animal was placed in Anchisauridae or its own family Thecodontosauridae alongside Agrosaurus.
facts.quote: Más tarde, se colocó en Anchisauridae o en su propio Thecodontosauridae junto con Agrosaurus.

facts.statement: Thecodontosaurus was originally included in the clade Prosauropoda, but recent suggestions propose that thecodontosaurs and their relatives were the primary group splitting from Prosauropods and Sauropods.
facts.quote: Originalmente fue incluido en el clado Prosauropoda pero más recientemente se ha sugerido que el tecodontosaurio y sus relativos fueron prioridad de la fractura Prosaurópodo-Saurópodo.

facts.statement: New reconstructions show that the neck of Thecodontosaurus is proportionally shorter than in more advanced ancient sauropodomorphs.
facts.quote: Nuevas reconstrucciones muestran que su cuello es proporcionalmente más corto que en sauropodomorfos antiguos más avanzados.

facts.statement: Thecodontosaurus is the best-known most primitive representative of sauropodomorph dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Thecodontosaurus es el representante más primitivo que mejor se conoce de dinosaurios sauropodomorfos.

facts.statement: The parent group of the genus Thecodontosaurus is Sauropodomorpha.
facts.quote: Parent group: Sauropodomorpha

facts.statement: Thecodontosaurus belongs to the class Saurischia.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia

facts.statement: There are 14 recorded fossil occurrences of Thecodontosaurus in the Paleobiology Database.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 14
